messages:
morgan: Heads-up — ran into a weird route match where tenant header + route pin picked a model alias that is NOT compatible with the runtime quantization. app errored with invalid KV cache shape. anyone seen this?
leah: ugh. which header? tenant or x-model-alias?
sam: most of our routing rules are header-first, then path, then query. but we added a soft-pin that can override alias selection depending on quota. could be ordering.
morgan: header was `x-tenant-model` (custom tenant header). route config had `soft_pin: alias:rdw-chat-7b:v2` and a compatibility constraint `requires:int8-kv-shape=v1`. runtime expects v2 kv layout.
ira: can you paste the rule snippet?
morgan: ```json
{
  "match": {"headers.x-tenant-model": "^acct-123$"},
  "actions": [
    {"type": "soft_pin", "alias": "rdw-chat-7b:v2"},
    {"type": "quota_check", "policy": "tenant-low"}
  ]
}
```
leah: oh — `soft_pin` intentionally only suggests an alias, not force. but our decider may fallback to a pinned model variant based on quota which currently resolves to a different alias with incompatible kernel.
sam: two separate problems: (1) rule evaluation precedence is under-documented in console, (2) compatibility checks happen post-resolve instead of during routing. we should validate alias compatibility before committing a route decision.
console-ux: for (1) — agree. users never know which rule matched when multiple apply. proposal: show the final matched rule + explanation in the request trace panel. something like: "Matched rule #42: header match -> soft_pin rdw-chat-7b:v2; but quota forced fallback to rdw-chat-7b:v1 (incompatible)."
ira: for (2) we could add a preflight step in the gateway: when a candidate alias is selected, run a quick compatibility check against runtime capabilities (kv-shape, quantization flags). if incompat, try next candidate or trigger fallback policy.
morgan: that would have prevented this. currently the gateway hands the alias to the runtime and runtime fails. it's noisy for customers.
sam: there's also the UX question: do we surface compatibility mismatches to customers or silently fallback? I think we must surface as a warning + fallback, because silent fallback changes semantics.
leah: agree. add telemetry: emit events `route.decision.candidate` and `route.decision.incompatible` with alias, reason, and final alias. that helps Optimize to detect regressions.
ira: implementation note: cheap checks only — compare model metadata vectors (kv-shape, block-size, quantization flags) in the catalog. no heavy binary loads.
console-ux: new trace event should show: matched-rule-id, chosen-alias, final-alias, reason-codes. UX can highlight when final != chosen. 
morgan: quick workaround — flip the soft_pin to `hard_pin` for acct-123 so it never falls back. but we shouldn't recommend hard-pinning everywhere.
sam: careful: hard_pin might violate quota routing expectations and cause capacity churn. prefer fixing evaluation order + preflight.
leah: action items: (1) eng-platform: add preflight compatibility check in gateway (ira + sam) (2) console: add matched-rule trace UI (console-ux) (3) telemetry: add `route.decision.*` events (leah) (4) run a scan of existing route rules for soft_pin -> alias combos with known incompat flags (morgan)
ira: I can prototype preflight check this week. will add a small cache for model metadata lookup.
console-ux: I'll mock the trace UI and show a sample infobar: "Routing chose rdw-chat-7b:v2 but fallback to rdw-chat-7b:v1 due to quota; incompatibility detected — model outputs may differ."
morgan: perfect. can we also add a dev flag `--strict-route-validation` so test envs fail fast? would help product teams.
sam: yes, add it to gateway bootstrap flags. default off for now.
deploy-bot: deploy queued by @ira for branch `route-preflight-proto` on staging. build 4521 -> started. :rocket:
ops-bot: FYI telemetry schema PR opened: https://git.redwood/schemas/+/234 (leah)
morgan: thanks all. will start the compatibility scan and ping if I find other tenants affected. :thumbsup:
